cards.headline: Free National Day long weekend entry to Science Centre S’pore; camera made just for children
bullets: Science Centre Singapore offers free entry for citizens and PRs from Aug 8 to 10.
The ocean-themed SG Science Fest includes a shipwreck mystery quest and robot vs hawker show.
Families can enjoy water fights and games, so remember to bring a change of clothes.
A new camera for kids, myFirst Camera Insta Lux, prints photos instantly.
The camera costs $229 and is available at Popular Bookstores and online.

cards.headline: More than 20 weekend flights between S’pore and southern China cancelled amid Typhoon Noul
bullets: Over 20 flights between Singapore and Hong Kong or southern China were cancelled this weekend.
Typhoon Noul caused the cancellations, hitting China's Guangdong province.
More than 340,000 people in Guangdong were moved to safety.
Hong Kong raised its storm alert to the second-highest level.

cards.headline: Former entertainment lawyer and Beam Artistes founder Samuel Seow dies at 53
bullets: Entertainment lawyer Samuel Seow died of a heart attack at 53.
He founded talent agency Beam Artistes, which managed male pageants.
Seow was previously disbarred for professional misconduct.
He was also jailed for assaulting his niece and another employee.

cards.headline: ‘If we can’t have a good marriage, at least have a good divorce’: S’pore man on amicable split
bullets: Nearly one in five civil couples used the new 'divorce by mutual agreement' option in 2025.
This new divorce reason allows couples to split without blaming each other.
A man shared how he and his wife used this option to end their marriage amicably.
Lawyers say this method reduces conflict and helps couples co-parent better.

cards.headline: Dad got healthy, gave up bad habits to donate liver to son with rare condition
bullets: A father gave up drinking and bad habits to donate part of his liver to his son.
His son, Isaiah, needed a transplant due to a rare genetic disorder called Alagille syndrome.
Isaiah was diagnosed with the condition at age two and was very weak.
His mother was initially set to donate but could not due to spleen issues.
The father's successful donation offers his son a chance at a healthy future.

cards.headline: Why every senior should strength train – and it's not just to prevent falls
bullets: New research links weak muscles in seniors to a lower ability to fight cancer.
Muscle loss, called sarcopenia, starts after age 50 and speeds up yearly.
Strength training can help seniors build muscle and boost their body's cancer-fighting power.
Simple exercises can help seniors regain strength, balance, and independence.
It's never too late for older adults to start strength training for better health.

cards.headline: She sold her house to save Mag’s. Nearly 30 years on, the Singapore restaurant is still evolving
bullets: Owner sold her house to save Mag's restaurant during the 1997 Asian financial crisis.
Mag's restaurant has been around for almost 30 years, starting as a wine bar.
The restaurant has moved locations twice and is now at 82 Neil Road.
Despite challenges, the owner remains passionate about the business and its wine selection.

cards.headline: More job tasters, credits to explore hobbies: SG Youth Plan aims to reach over half a million youths in 5 years
bullets: Over half a million young people will be reached by the new SG Youth Plan in five years.
The plan offers credits for youths to explore hobbies and interests.
An independent living pilot will offer discounted co-living spaces for those aged 21 to 35.
Up to S$20 million will fund 3,000 youth-led projects over the next five years.

cards.headline: Born with hearing loss, she found her voice on the musical theatre stage
bullets: Sabrina Wong, who has moderate-to-severe hearing loss, will graduate with a musical theatre degree.
She struggled with shyness and speech issues due to hearing loss from a young age.
Wong uses hearing aids daily to help her hear and communicate.
Performing on stage allows her to step out of her shy persona.
She found confidence and her voice through music, theatre, and speech therapy.

cards.headline: Marvel unveils Ghost Rider, Black Panther 3 at San Diego Comic-Con
bullets: Marvel announced Black Panther 3 and Ghost Rider movies coming in 2028.
Black Panther 3 will feature a new actor as T'Challa's son.
First footage from Avengers: Doomsday showed Doctor Doom defeating the Avengers.
Avengers: Doomsday is set to clash with the new Dune movie.

cards.headline: One Raffles Quay floated as possible divestment for Suntec Reit
bullets: One Raffles Quay might be sold by Suntec Reit.
The Reit manager said it's the lowest-yielding asset.
This is because the Reit pays income tax on it.
Suntec Reit is currently focused on selling Australian assets.
The Reit's earnings per unit rose by almost 25%.

cards.headline: Xpeng Mona L03: The Category A EV that could usher in robot helpers
bullets: The new Xpeng L03 car, also known as Mona L03 in China, went on sale in 65 markets globally.
It is expected to cost around S$200,000 with a Category A certificate in Singapore by late 2026.
The car features a sleek design, voice command system, and self-driving capabilities powered by AI chips.
XPeng aims for the L03 to be a 'physical AI' product, part of a future vision including robots and flying cars.
XPeng's global sales dropped by over 15% in the first half of 2026, making the L03's success crucial.

cards.headline: Range Rover GT: The secrets behind the brand’s strangest car ever
bullets: Range Rover is launching its first-ever electric sedan, the GT, which looks very different from its usual SUVs.
Despite its low, car-like shape, the GT is designed to handle off-road driving like other Range Rovers.
The new electric GT will feature a minimalist interior with new materials and two large screens.
The car is expected to have a driving range of over 600 km and will be revealed around September.

cards.headline: US mortgage rates rise, extending gains for third straight week
bullets: US mortgage rates hit 6.58% for a 30-year fixed loan, up for the third week.
Rising US mortgage rates are making it harder for people to buy homes.
Home prices in the US saw their biggest yearly jump in over three years.
Higher gas prices and inflation concerns are straining buyers' finances in the US.

cards.headline: 2 girls, 14, found dead in M'sia after apparently falling from height, were close friends from same school
bullets: Two 14-year-old schoolmates were found dead in Ipoh, Malaysia.
They were believed to have fallen from a tall building.
Police found no signs of foul play so far.
The girls had left school voluntarily that afternoon.

cards.headline: S'porean seniors have more savings to spend on health, but 'unnecessary treatments' could drive up costs: Ong Ye Kung
bullets: Seniors have more savings for health, but could face higher costs from unnecessary treatments.
Health Minister warns against over-servicing and costly, unneeded medical procedures.
Anxious patients might get too many scans, driving up healthcare expenses.
Government seeks stronger partnerships with private sector to keep healthcare affordable.

cards.headline: Woman in Taiwan, 31, drugged & suffocated her sons, 8 & 3, charged with murder
bullets: A 31-year-old mother in Taiwan is charged with murder for allegedly drugging and suffocating her two young sons.
The incident happened in January when the woman allegedly gave her sons, aged eight and three, sleep medication.
She then reportedly smothered them to death while on a phone call with a friend.
The friend found the children unresponsive and called the police, but they could not be saved.
The mother was uncooperative and emotionally unstable during police questioning.

cards.headline: We Checked Out The F1 Exhibition In SG, Featuring Iconic Race Cars, Interactive Stations & Exclusive Merch
bullets: The Formula 1 Exhibition is now in Singapore, the first stop in Asia.
See iconic F1 cars driven by champions like Prost and Vettel.
Try out an F1 simulator and design your own helmet.
Learn about the history and design evolution of Formula 1 cars.

cards.headline: LaLaport BBCC Has A New Modern Bus Terminal For KL-SG Routes, With Free WiFi & Luggage Lockers
bullets: A new bus terminal at LaLaport BBCC in KL now offers direct routes to Singapore.
The hub has free WiFi, luggage lockers, and a comfortable waiting lounge.
It's connected to shops and eateries within LaLaport BBCC for convenience.
The terminal is also a short walk to Hang Tuah LRT and Monorail stations.
